character_facts: Othon is dying from poisonous gas exposure and wants Aghnar hardened for vengeance.
Aghnar is Othon's son and is able to defeat his father in single combat.
Aghnar is motivated by avenging Honorata.
Kiowata is a floating ape identified as a Magon.
Kiowata can speak and is described as having a soul.
Princess Oda is described as beautiful and genetically important to the Shabda-Oud plan.
Aghnar falls in love with Oda immediately after seeing her holovid.
continuity_links: This page explicitly recaps events from earlier installments rather than advancing a new scene.
It sets up Aghnar's next movement toward Amadis and Princess Oda.
It connects the deaths and trials involving Othon and Honorata to the ongoing conflict with the Shabda-Oud.
dialogue_meaning: There is no character dialogue; the page provides editorial recap narration summarizing prior events and stakes.
The narration explains Aghnar's recent trials, Othon's death, the threat posed by the Shabda-Oud, and Aghnar's new goal involving Princess Oda.
locations: a refuge planet dominated by powerful gravity
lore_facts: The Castakas have been living in hiding on a planet marked by powerful gravity.
That planet features giant mushrooms, floating apes, and flat carnivorous animals.
Othon dispatched spy-needles into space to gather information about the Shabda-Oud witches.
A Cetacyborg can be destroyed in a way that releases poisonous gas.
A Magon can be a floating ape that speaks and possesses a soul.
There exists a prophecy concerning a little white ape leading the Magon to the Diamond Planet.
A Cetacyborg can be taken over or controlled with aid from the floating apes.
The Shabda-Oud seek a hermaphrodite and believe Princess Oda's genes can help produce one.
A holovid recording can be used to show Oda remotely.
Amadis is a place associated with Oda and her line of suitors.
plot_events: The Castakas are said to have taken refuge on a planet with extreme gravity, giant mushrooms, floating apes, and predatory flat animals.
Spy-needles sent into space by Othon are expected to return information that can help locate the Shabda-Oud witches.
Othon is dying from poison gas exposure caused by the destruction of a Cetacyborg.
Othon demands that his son Aghnar kill him in single combat so the son will be strong enough to avenge Honorata.
Aghnar defeats his father through both intellect and force.
Aghnar saves a floating ape from being seized after a fall.
The ape, identified as Kiowata, is revealed to be a Magon who can speak and has a soul.
Aghnar and Kiowata ascend to the tops of the giant mushrooms, where Aghnar confronts and defeats the Magon leader.
This victory fulfills a prophecy about a little white ape leading the Magon to the Diamond Planet.
Aghnar learns where the Shabda-Oud are and uses a Cetacyborg with help from the floating apes.
He overcomes three Shabda-Oud pilots and learns their mission: to abduct Princess Oda because her genes can produce the hermaphrodite sought by the witches.
After seeing a holovid of Oda, Aghnar falls in love with her and sets out alone and unarmed for Amadis to join her suitors.
